articles.title: Louisiana Court Order Gives Players Signed by NFL Teams a Shot at Returning to College Sports
articles.summary: Several athletes, including some who signed contracts with NFL teams, were granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court that would make them eligible to return to college athletics, ESPN reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Several athletes, including some who signed contracts with NFL teams, were granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court that would make them eligible to return to college athletics, ESPN reported Wednesday.

Former Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson (Seattle Seahawks), former Florida and LSU pass rusher Jack Pyburn (Tampa Bay Buccaneers) and ex-Mississippi starters Dae'Quan Wright (Cleveland Browns) and Wydett Williams (Arizona Cardinals) are on NFL rosters and were part of the lawsuit.

NFL teams are deep into training camp, and rosters have to be cut to 53 players by Aug. 30. Many who don't make those clubs could look for a fallback plan in college football, barring a successful appeal by the NCAA.

According to ESPN, 16 football players were part of the lawsuit that included 33 athletes across several sports who are seeking a fifth year of eligibility.

The NCAA has been dealt a series of legal setbacks regarding its eligibility rules.

"Courts across the country granting relief to ineligible athletes who already had every opportunity to compete in college — sometimes without even having a hearing — are failing to appreciate the destabilizing effect their rulings are having on college sports," Tim Buckley, NCAA senior vice president of external affairs, said in a statement.

"The lawyers bringing these cases seemingly won't be satisfied until every professional athlete can treat college sports as a fallback option, regardless of the opportunities it strips from those who will never have a chance to begin their collegiate sports experience."

On July 31, a federal court in Denver ruled that all high school class of 2022 athletes who exhausted their fourth season of college eligibility this spring are eligible for a fifth season this academic year.

That decision came a little more than a month after the NCAA passed a rule that gives athletes five years to complete five seasons of competition, starting with those who enroll in the fall of 2027. The Colorado ruling eliminated the waiting period.

articles.title: Champions League 2026-27: When is the league phase draw and who is in each pot?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains when the league phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League is, as well as looking at who is in each pot
articles.body:
The league phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League campaign takes place on Thursday, 27 August at 17:00 BST in Monaco.

A total of 36 teams will enter that stage of the competition and while 29 teams qualified at the end of last season, the remaining seven places are decided by qualifiers that will conclude next week.

In the league phase, each team will face eight different teams once, with four home matches and four away matches.

For the draw, the 36 teams will be placed into four pots with one being the highest-ranked and four being the lowest. The pot placements are based on the club's Uefa club coefficient ranking from the five-season period ending at the conclusion of 2025-26.

Each team will face two teams from each of the four pots and cannot face a team from the same country as themselves.

The teams who finish in the top eight will qualify for the Champions League's round of 16. Those between ninth and 24th will enter the play-off knockout round. The 12 teams ranked between 25th and 36th will exit the competition when the league phase is concluded.

While the final seven spots in the league phase of the 2026-27 Champions League are yet to be decided, the other 29 teams are confirmed. The majority of those 29 already know which pot they will be in.

The nine teams in each of the first two pots are confirmed.

Premier League clubs Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal all feature in pot one alongside back-to-back Champions League winners Paris St-Germain, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Inter Milan, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

Aston Villa and Manchester United both return to the Champions League this season after not featuring last term. They are in pot two with Borussia Dortmund, Roma, Sporting, Porto, Club Brugge, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

With the remaining places up for grabs split across pots three and four, some teams do still have uncertainty as to which pot they could end up in.

Feyenoord, Lille, Napoli, RB Leipzig, Villarreal, Shakhtar Donetsk and Galatasaray are all guaranteed to enter the draw in pot three.

The winners of the play-off knockout round match between Fenerbahce and Lyon are also guaranteed to enter pot three.

VfB Stuttgart, Como and Lens are all guaranteed to enter in pot four. The winners of the qualifying ties between Levski Sofia and AEK Athens, Slovan Bratislava and Celje, and Hapoel Be'er Sheva and Sabah, will follow them into that pot.

The final four spots are contested between the ties involving NEC Nijmegen and Bodo/Glimt, Dinamo Zagreb and Viking, Celtic and LASK, as well as Slavia Prague.

Bodo/Glimt will take the one spot remaining in pot three, should they beat NEC Nijmegen. If that happens, Slavia Prague and the winners of the other two qualifying ties will all enter the draw in pot four.

If NEC Nijmegen win, Dinamo Zagreb would have the next best club coefficient rating. For them to enter pot three, they need Bodo/Glimt to lose and for themselves to get past Viking.

While Celtic and Slavia Prague are level on their five-year and last season's club coefficient ratings, Celtic scored more ratings points than Slavia Prague in the 2024-25 term. If Celtic beat LASK and Bodo/Glimt and Dinamo Zagreb both lose, they will take the final pot three spot.

If Bodo/Glimt, Dinamo Zagreb and Celtic all lose, the final pot four place will go to Slavia Prague.

articles.title: La nueva realidad de Marc Guiu: renuncia a su dorsal en el Chelsea para redefinir su futuro
articles.standfirst: Marc Guiu decide quedarse sin dorsal en el Chelsea para valorar las diferentes opciones de Inglaterra, Italia y España que tiene para salir de Stamford Bridge
articles.summary: El Chelsea deja sin dorsal a Marc Guiu, delantero español de 20 años que tasa en 29 millones euros
articles.body: Marc Guiu, uno de los candidatos ser el '9' de España en la próxima década, ha decidido quedarse sin dorsal en el Chelsea de Xabi Alonso para para valorar las diferentes opciones de Inglaterra, Italia y España que tiene para salir de Stamford Bridge. "Mi pensamiento sobre Guiu es, ¿cómo lo dejó ir el Barcelona? El Barça cometió un error increíble con Marc. Mi pensamiento sobre Guiu es, ¿cómo lo dejó ir el Barcelona? El Barça cometió un error increíble con Marc. Este chico dentro de dos años podría ser un número 9 establecido e increíble. Tiene todas las cosas que no puedes enseñar... y juega con una sonrisa en la cara", dijo Joe Cole en 2024 en TNT Sports. El número 38 la que ha renunciado Marc Guiu lo tiene ahora Tosin Adarabioyo. Marc Guiu, que sólo tiene 20 años, ha sido tasado los 'blues' en 29 millones de euros y le quedan tres temporadas de contrato por delante con el Chelsea. Durante su etapa en Stamford Bridge el delantero catalán ha sumado 7 goles en 24 partidos oficiales, destacando especialmente en partidos de la Conference League. "No soy yo, es Dios", compartió Guiu en Instagram tras marcar su primer gol con el Chelsea. 11 partidos (402 minutos), 1 gol y 1 asistencia la temporada 2025/2026 y 11 partidos (371 minutos) y 6 goles el curso 2024/2025. En agosto de 2025 fue cedido al Sunderland de la EFL Championship, pero tras tres partidos (1 gol) y 25 días tuvo que volver de emergencia al Chelsea tras la grave lesión de Liam Delap y la salida de Nico Jackson al Bayern. "Marc está de vuelta. La razón por la que está de vuelta es porque la intención es usarlo. Necesita hacer las cosas mejor y mejorar, pero seguro que lo vamos a usar", explicó su entonces entrenador Enzo Maresca. Tras renunciar a su dorsal el Sunderland podría ser uno de los posibles destinos para Guiu, por el que también podrían haber mostrado interés Real Sociedad, Sevilla, Coventry City, Ipswich Town y el fútbol saudí.  Marc Guiu (Sant Celoni, 2006), canterano del Barça habló en Esports RAC1 en su primera entrevista tras dejar Barcelona. "No me arrepiento de haber dejado el Barça. Al final es una cosa que yo decidí para mi carrera. Creo que era la mejor opción y todavía lo sigo creyendo, y ahora a disfrutar de la Premier y del Chelsea", explicó el punta catalán en el programa 'Tú Dirás' desde la concentración de la selección sub 21 de España. Marc Guiu se estrenó como goleador en el Barcelona con 17 años y 9 meses a los 33 segundos de saltar al campo. El prometedor delantero español tuvo la posibilidad de renovar con el Barça con un salario de dos millones brutos al año para las próximas cuatro temporadas.  El delantero internacional en categoría inferiores con España explicó sobre su salida al Chelsea que "me llamó Maresca y me dijo que confiaba en mí y el proyecto deportivo era increíble. Y no me arrepiento de esta decisión". "¿Si hablé con Hansi Flick en ese momento? No. Me envió algún mensaje pero no llegué a hablar con él. Sinceramente. Me dijo, cuando estábamos en el playoff con el filial, que me fuese muy bien", contó.

articles.body: Marcus Rashford, que ha vuelto al Manchester United tras su cesión de una temporada en el F.C. Barcelona, ha pedido poder jugar al fútbol sin que su "nombre se mencione a diario". Sería genial poder centrarme y jugar al fútbol sin que se mencione mi nombre todos los días". articles.title: Max Verstappen signs new F1 contract with Red Bull until 2030
articles.summary: Four-time F1 World Drivers’ Champion’s new deal puts to rest rumours that he would exit the team at the end of 2028.
articles.body:
Multiple Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed a new contract with Red Bull Racing until the end of 2030, the team announced, ending speculation over his future in the sport.

“Four more years of full send. We are delighted to announce that Max has signed a contract extension with the team until the end of 2030,” Red Bull said on X on Thursday.

The news came with preparations in full swing for Verstappen’s home race this Sunday, the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort, and will delight his thousands of orange-clad fans.

Verstappen is one of the most successful Formula One drivers of all time, dominating the sport with four consecutive world championships from 2021.

But results have been harder to come by this season, with the 28-year-old failing to see a chequered flag in the first half of the year and sitting sixth in the drivers’ championship.

“This commitment is about more than continuing an already extraordinary alliance,” the team said in its statement.

“It is a powerful statement of mutual trust and ambition – and a shared decision to shape the future together.”

The uncompetitive nature of the Red Bull car this year has led many to speculate that the mercurial Dutchman could switch to another team or even leave Formula One entirely.

But Verstappen said he was keen to get the team back to winning ways.

“We have the best people and I’m excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again,” he was quoted as saying.

The news adds even more spice to the last-ever edition of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

Verstappen was unbeatable on his home track, winning the first three editions since it was reintroduced to the circuit in 2021.

But he has since been chasing McLaren in his own back yard, with Papaya drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri claiming the last two races.

Verstappen is expected to don a special helmet for the occasion, inspired by the famous blue Delft pottery.

The promoters decided not to continue racing at Zandvoort, partly due to uncertainty over Verstappen’s future given his importance for the popularity of the event.

“I have always said it: The team is like a second family for me and I feel very at home,” said Verstappen.

“I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely,” added Verstappen, using his trademark phrase.

articles.title: El Inter dice 'no' por Lautaro
articles.standfirst: El equipo italiano declara intransferible al delantero
articles.summary: El equipo italiano declara intransferible al delante
articles.body: El Barcelona sigue trabajando en busca de un delantero centro. Es la principal petición de Hans Flick. No es de ahora, sino desde el final de la temporada anterior, cuando se confirmó de manera definitiva la salida de Robert Lewandowski. Sin el polaco, unido a las bajas de Ferran y Rashford, al técnico alemán le faltan muchos goles y, por ello, necesita un goleador en su plantilla. Todas las miras están puestas en Julián Álvarez. Es el gran objetivo que se marcó la Dirección Deportiva. Sin embargo, pasan las semanas y no se avanza en esta operación. El Barcelona está a la espera de un movimiento de Julián para desbloquear la negociación con el Atlético. Este no se produce y todo está en punto muerto. El tiempo se acaba porque estamos a dos semanas del cierre del mercado. El Barça no espera con los brazos cruzados y Deco ya tiene alternativas por si no se concreta lo de Julián. Uno de los candidatos a venir al Barcelona es Lautaro Martínez. El director deportivo del Barcelona ha comenzado a trabajar en el tema. Ya hubo conversaciones con el entorno del jugador para conocer la disponibilidad del argentino. Por aquí no habría problema: si se presenta la oportunidad, Lautaro iría al Camp Nou. El equipo italiano no quiere desprenderse de su principal estrella y ha declarado intransferible al delantero. Habrá que esperar a ver si las negociaciones podrían hacer pensárselo mejor a un Inter que por ahora no quiere oír hablar de una posible salida de su mejor jugador.  No es el único jugador que está en el punto de mira por si falla lo de Julián Álvarez. También se está siguiendo a dos futbolistas del Villarreal: Mikautadze y Ayoze. Son dos jugadores del agrado de Flick y con un perfil diferente, tanto por sus cualidades como jugadores como por el precio de cada uno. El primero de ellos es mucho más caro, con una cláusula de rescisión de 78 millones. El Villarreal, que ya sabe del interés del Barcelona, está pendiente de que el club azulgrana tome una decisión definitiva, ya que, si se lleva a uno de sus jugadores, deberá buscar en el mercado un sustituto. Así que todo está en el aire mientras no se resuelva de manera definitiva la posible incorporación de Julián. En el Barcelona piensan que las palabras del Cholo, en las que respaldó a la afición que gritó contra el delantero en el partido del miércoles, pueden precipitar una reacción del delantero.

articles.title: SEC Football Preview and Predictions for the 2026 Season
articles.summary: Is the SEC the nation's deepest conference? Absolutely, it should be once again. But is it the best? Well, anyone who says that would have a hard time backing it up.
articles.body:
Is the SEC the nation's deepest conference? Absolutely, it should be once again. But is it the best? Well, anyone who says that would have a hard time backing it up.

The Big Ten could just use the old playground comeback: "Scoreboard!"

The past three national champions all hail from that rival league to the north with Michigan, Ohio State, and last year's unbeaten Indiana Hoosiers hoisting the trophy. Before that run, the SEC had won 13 of the past 17 titles.

Now, though, the league with the most NFL talent year-in and year-out is looking to get back to the podium. It's not going to get any easier, either, with the conference moving to a nine-game schedule and the argument that the teams "just beat up on themselves" strengthening.

The SEC is, however, loaded with potentially elite teams once again. Texas, Georgia, Ole Miss and Texas A&M will be very good. Others like Oklahoma, LSU, Alabama, and possibly even Tennessee and South Carolina could be strong, too.

But can one of them reach the top? Let's take a look at what to expect from southern-fried football in '26.

It's impossible to zero in on just who is going to steal the show in the SEC. There's just so much talent, and it's an inexact science as last year's predictions of Garrett Nussmeier, DJ Lagway and LaNorris Sellers fell flat.

Sellers is back under center at South Carolina, and Arch Manning overcame a rough start a season ago at Texas to have a nice season, so both of those guys could flash. Georgia's Gunner Stockton , Oklahoma's John Mateer and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed are household-name field generals, and there are high hopes for Sam Leavitt at LSU.

But Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss is going to set the pace at quarterback, and Kewan Lacy forms one of the league's top offensive duos with the signal-caller.

Still, though, there are so many weapons across the league like runners Ahmad Hardy (Missouri), DeSean Bishop (Tennessee), Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown (Texas) and Jadan Baugh (Florida). Catching passes will be some of the nation's top weapons like Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo (Texas), Ryan Coleman-Williams (Alabama), TreyDez Green (LSU), Mario Craver (Texas A&M), Isaiah Satenga (Oklahoma), Braylon Staley and Mike Matthews (Tennessee) and Nyck Harbor (South Carolina).

Road-grading linemen include Trevor Goosby at Texas, Mizzou's Cayden Green, South Carolina's Jacarrius Peak , LSU's Jordan Seaton and returning Georgia standouts Earnest Greene III , Dontrell Glover and Drew Bobo . Tennessee's line should be strong, too, led by David Sanders Jr .

Defensive playmakers Colin Simmons and Rasheem Biles (Texas), Dylan Stewart (South Carolina), Princewill Umanmielen and Whit Weeks (LSU), Xavier Atkins (Auburn), DJ Hicks and Marcus Ratcliffe (Texas A&M), Arion Carter and Xavier Gilliam (Tennessee), Will Echoles and Suntarine Perkins (Ole Miss) will be elite.

Alabama ( Zabien Brown , Bray Hubbard , Keon Sabb ), Georgia ( KJ Bolden , Ellis Robinson IV , Khalil Barnes ), Oklahoma ( Eli Bowen and Peyton Bowen ) and LSU ( DJ Pickett , Ty Benefield ) have superstars in the secondary too.

Once again, the talent in the SEC is absurd.

Without a doubt, the biggest thing to watch this year is the league moving to nine conference games and how that will affect the title contenders.

Will they be more beat up? More prepared? Potentially, would an extra loss impact an SEC team that otherwise would have made the College Football Playoff with a cupcake win instead of the setback?

It's obviously a major money-maker for Greg Sankey and Co. to add the extra game, but the residual effects are at least worth monitoring.

OK, we know Lake Pontchartrain is 50 or so miles from Baton Rouge, but you get the point. Lane Kiffin left Ole Miss for hated rival LSU, and it's the biggest buzz in the league.

Everybody's got the Bayou Bengals' September 19 trip to Oxford on the schedule of must-watch TV, and Kiffin went out and added major reinforcements to the Tigers roster through the transfer portal and recruiting. Whether it's enough to turn LSU into an immediate contender remains to be seen.

The expectations are massive, though. When you make a move with these shockwaves, you want results right now. Everybody's watching.

Everybody's talking about Kiffin, of course. But this is the most turnover in the SEC coaching ranks in the modern era.

An astounding six teams changed head coaches – three of those coming from the AAC. Alex Golesh left South Florida for Auburn, Jon Sumrall exited Tulane for Florida and Ryan Silverfield headed up the road from Memphis to Arkansas.

Will Stein returns to his home state of Kentucky to coach the Wildcats, leaving his offensive coordinator perch at Oregon. And Pete Golding, who took over before the postseason run for the departed Kiffin, inherits a roster goldmine at Ole Miss.

Preseason prognostications indicate the league title could run through the Lone Star State.

Texas is deep, talented and the likely favorite in the league. Texas A&M is also coming off a playoff run and fortified some gaps through the transfer portal.

Georgia, Ole Miss, Oklahoma and others will have something to say about who's going to come out on top, but both of the SEC teams from Texas are loaded.

Several SEC teams will probably stake their hopes on youngsters at quarterback.

At Alabama, it's either going to be Keelon Russell or Austin Mack, so if Russell (a former 5-star redshirt freshman with very limited experience) wins the job, he'll be handed the keys to a potential title contender.

In the Volunteer State, it's going to be either true freshman Faizon Brandon or redshirt freshman George Macintyre calling the shots for Josh Heupel at Tennessee, and Vanderbilt likely will replace Diego Pavia with former 5-star true freshman Jared Curtis.

Then, at Florida, it's going to either be redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr., or Georgia Tech sophomore transfer Aaron Philo. Those are some good programs with uncertainty leading the way.

Tier 1: Texas, Georgia, Ole Miss, Texas A&M, LSU

The expected top five in the league are pretty clear right now, but everything after that is just a matter of how you think it's going to shake out. Also, if a couple of young quarterbacks hit in that second tier, things could change.

Texas is deep, and even though new defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has some turnover on that side of the ball, the Longhorns outfitted the roster through the portal with massive reinforcements.

At Georgia, titles are the benchmark, and coach Kirby Smart has a dynamic defense once again and a veteran quarterback in Gunner Stockton. He's won national titles with that same formula.

After last year's deep College Football Playoff run, folks in Oxford think this could be the year the Rebels break the SEC championship game drought, and oh what fun would that be in the first full year of the post-Lane Kiffin era? Speaking of Kiffin, he's got a roster at LSU built to win right now.

Texas A&M is kind of laying in the weeds with all this Longhorn buzz, but don't sleep on the Aggies, either. There are several teams in this group that can win it all.

Tier 2: Oklahoma, Alabama, South Carolina, Tennessee

Fans of two teams in this group aren't going to be happy to be here, and two others will be thrilled.

At Alabama, it's all about finding a viable running game and the right quarterback to lead Kalen DeBoer's offense. The defense is going to be one of the nation's best and terrific at all levels. But there have been offensive issues, and now they're replacing Ty Simpson? Questions abound.

Oklahoma made it to the playoffs a year ago with a magical run through a gauntlet schedule, and the Sooners return John Mateer at quarterback and playmakers on both sides of the ball. But can they catch magic twice? Sooners fans think they're a playoff lock.

For South Carolina and Tennessee, the season's a toss-up. The Vols have a lot to like on that roster if a young quarterback steps up. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has transformed things on that side of the ball.

In Columbia, it's now or never for Shane Beamer, but with LaNorris Sellers a prime pick for a rebound campaign with Kendal Briles calling the plays, a turnaround could be in the cards.

With six new coaches leading the charge in the league, there are really just a couple of coaches with warm bottoms entering the season.

Of course, if they have poor years, Tennessee's Josh Heupel and Alabama's Kalen DeBoer could possibly exit 2026 sweating a bit, but neither of those guys are in any danger of losing their jobs in the next calendar year. A couple of their peers are.

Last year, South Carolina was a College Football Playoff sleeper and crashed to a 4-8 record, winning just one SEC game and blowing a massive late-season lead against Texas A&M.

Now, after hiring Kendal Briles, Beamer, quarterback LaNorris Sellers and Co. are again on many minds as a possible turnaround team. The Gamecocks have talent, and they've got several opportunities to grab statement wins in the national spotlight.

If they don't, they'll be looking for a new coach. Beamer won't survive another losing season.

Mississippi State made it to a bowl game with a losing record a season ago and was promptly dismantled by Wake Forest. It was a disastrous end to a frustrating season.

Early on, the Bulldogs were the league's tough-luck loser.

After starting 4-0, MSU lost 41-34 at home against Tennessee in overtime, then after a lopsided loss to Texas A&M, fell 23-21 at Florida and took Texas to the brink in Starkville before losing 45-38 in overtime.

They fell apart after that, ending the year (following a close win over Arkansas) getting dismantled by Georgia, Missouri, Ole Miss and Wake Forest.

What does that mean for Lebby? He's coaching in a traditionally tough place to win. But 7-18 isn't going to cut it for long, and the Bulldogs aren't expected to make much noise this year, either.

Sep. 5: Clemson at LSU, Baylor vs. Auburn (in Atlanta)

Sep. 6: Louisville vs. Ole Miss (in Nashville)

Sep. 12: Oklahoma at Michigan, Tennessee at Georgia Tech, Ohio State at Texas, Arkansas at Utah

Nov. 28: Georgia Tech at Georgia, Louisville at Kentucky, South Carolina at Clemson

College football hits us with some nice little warmups during Week 1 to whet our appetites with Clemson traveling to LSU as well as Baylor meeting Auburn in Atlanta, and we'll know a bit about both sets of Tigers after those tilts. Louisville and Ole Miss meeting in Nashville is a sneaky showdown, too.

Everybody wants to watch Ohio State head to Austin to take on Texas in a rematch of national title contenders. Oklahoma heads to the Big House to face Michigan in another SEC/Big Ten showdown, and Tennessee travels to Atlanta to face Georgia Tech. Ryan Silverfield's first game at Arkansas will be in Salt Lake City against Utah in a tough test, too.

After those first two weekends, though, all we have in the way of marquee out-of-conference matchups is Florida State coming to Alabama in Week 3. Rivalry weekend gives us the next taste of non-SEC grudge matches.

Sep. 19: LSU at Ole Miss, Florida at Auburn

Sep. 26: Oklahoma at Georgia, Texas A&M at LSU, South Carolina at Alabama, Texas at Tennessee

Oct. 10: Georgia at Alabama, Texas A&M at Missouri, Texas vs. Oklahoma (Dallas)

Oct. 17: Missouri at Ole Miss, Alabama at Tennessee

Oct. 24: Ole Miss at Texas, Texas A&M at Alabama, Tennessee at South Carolina

Oct. 31: Florida vs. Georgia (Jacksonville)

Nov. 7: Georgia at Ole Miss, Texas at Missouri, Texas A&M at South Carolina, Alabama at LSU

Nov. 14: Missouri at Georgia, Texas at LSU, Tennessee at Texas A&M, Ole Miss at Oklahoma

Nov. 21: Georgia at South Carolina, Texas A&M at Oklahoma, LSU at Tennessee

Nov. 28: Oklahoma at Missouri, Auburn at Alabama

It's almost as if the SEC scheduling gods knew we simply couldn't wait.

Right off the bat on September 19, we've got the game we all want to see: Lane Kiffin heading back to Oxford as LSU coach to take on the Ole Miss team he built into a playoff program a season ago. That game will captivate the entire nation, but it's only the beginning.

The very next weekend may be the biggest of the year as the Sooners head to Athens, the Aggies descend on Death Valley, South Carolina gets tested right away in Tuscaloosa and Texas enters a hostile Neyland Stadium environment.

Following a bit of a "down" weekend October 3, Georgia plays at Alabama the next weekend, and we get the Red River Rivalry, too. In a nine-game schedule, there are no cakewalks, and that means high-quality games for us fans every single weekend.

If you love SEC football, you'll get a heaping helping of it this year. Game after game of intensity dot the calendar all the way through October and November.

The easiest answer here perhaps would be Ole Miss, which returns potentially the nation's top quarterback (Trinidad Chambliss) and running back (Kewan Lacy) along with plenty of capable pass-catchers.

But losing coach Lane Kiffin and offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. to LSU won't be easy to replace, so those growing pains the team could face adjusting to new play-caller John David Baker could stunt the potency a bit.

That's why we're rolling with Texas here.

Sure, a season ago, it took Arch Manning more than half the season to get going, but coach Steve Sarkisian went out in the transfer portal and surrounded his budding star signal-caller with elite talent in what is sure to be his final season in Austin.

The biggest prize for Texas is former Auburn receiver Cam Coleman who may be the most physically gifted receiver in the nation. He will team with Ryan Wingo for an elite 1-2 punch.

Beating Alabama for former North Carolina State running back Hollywood Smothers and pairing him with former Arizona State game-breaker Raleek Brown gives the Longhorns a top-tier running back duo, too.

Add in an offensive line with a lot of strong pieces, and Texas is going to score a bunch of points.

This is where the SEC could truly flex this year.

It wouldn't be surprising to see retooled Texas, which added players like Rasheem Biles to a roster that already featured Colin Simmons, an Alabama unit full of returning talent, a hard-nosed Texas A&M group taking on the persona of head coach Mike Elko or an Oklahoma group that led the league a year ago be the top defensive dog.

We're rolling with Georgia here, though.

The Bulldogs are going to have to replace a bunch of starts up front alongside Gabe Harris Jr., but the second and third levels of Glenn Schumann's defense will be nationally stout. Elijah Griffin is a potential All-American inside.

Georgia also has a deep and talented linebacking corps that features Raylen Wilson and Chris Cole, both of whom could be first-round picks. However, Quintavius Johnson has just as much talent at the Jack spot, too.

On the back end, KJ Bolden and Ellis Robinson IV also have the potential to be the best players in the nation at their position, and there are other veterans all over the place like Khalil Barnes and Demello Jones.

Projected SEC Championship: Texas vs. Ole Miss

This is the year the Ole Miss Rebels break the streak and make it to their first SEC championship game. Doing so in the wake of the Lane Kiffin era's abrupt end will be extra sweet, too.

Coach Pete Golding's team will be 10-2 heading into the conference title game, making it to the title game after beating their old coach and besting UGA on November 7 in a rematch of last year's playoff game.

Unfortunately for the Rebels, they won't be able to get past a Texas juggernaut clicking at the end of the season on both sides of the ball.

Everybody thought the Longhorns were going to compete for all the marbles a season ago, but an early-season struggle proved too much for them to overcome, and despite coach Steve Sarkisian's pleas, the College Football Playoff committee kept them out of the final 12.

That won't happen again this year. The 'Horns defense will be clicking under first-year coordinator Will Muschamp, and the offense will score enough to get by a strong Ole Miss team, propelling them to the playoffs.

Don't worry, Rebs. Your team is going, too.

articles.title: B/R Football Writers' Bold Predictions for the 2026-27 Premier League
articles.summary: And on to the new season of the Premier League.
articles.body:
And on to the new season of the Premier League.

Football's most popular league begins anew on Friday as champions Arsenal begin the defense of their title. Will the Gunners retain their crown? Will opponents Coventry City beat the odds and avoid relegation this season?

Our team of Calum Rogers, Leo Collis and Nick Akerman provided the answers to those questions and more as they offered their bold predictions for the 2026-27 Premier League campaign.

Leo Collis: It should be Erling Haaland. Really, it should. But if we're going for bold predictions, why not pick a striker who scored just three Premier League goals during the whole of last season?

Of course, that description does Alexander Isak a disservice, considering he bagged 54 in 86 top-flight games for Newcastle United across three seasons. But his debut campaign with the Reds was nothing short of disastrous, losing time while being integrated into the XI, sharpening his fitness, and then breaking his leg just as it looked like he was starting to fit in.

That limited him to just 14 games and 702 minutes of action. However, it should be a much different story in 2026-27. Despite a slightly late start because of the World Cup, the Swede actually had a pre-season with the Reds this time around, allowing him to develop more chemistry with his teammates.

Isak has looked sharp in friendly fixtures, and if he can maintain his fitness, he should get back to the levels that saw him notch 21 goals and 23 goals in back-to-back Premier League seasons before his switch to Anfield.

Nick Akerman: This isn't bold in the slightest. I'm sorry. Maybe just offering a plain retort to Leo's argument can be considered bold in the context of this article? It's a cop-out, but I can't in good conscience put forward another player who will even get close to what I expect Haaland to score next season.

Perhaps that's the bold bit? I can realistically see Haaland scoring more than 30 goals, and nobody else even reaching 20. Let's go with that…Manchester City won't win the title, and Haaland will score 15 more than anybody else. Why not?

Calum Rogers: I did consider Igor Thiago and Alexander Isak here, but former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha summed this category up nicely on The Ripple Effect with James Lawrence Allcott : "You can say that Haaland's not gonna score as many, but who's gonna score more?"

And let's not pretend there aren't significant concerns around Haaland's competitors. Isak suffered a broken leg and other muscle issues last season, limiting his impact. Thiago, meanwhile, scored 22 goals last season, but just six of those came in 2026, and eight of his 22 tallies were penalties.

Even if City do fall off considerably under Maresca, it's still tough to imagine Haaland not being able to stay ahead of the competition. He hasn't scored fewer than 22 goals in a season since he was 18, though, so the bold prediction I (a coward) am willing to make is that Haaland will score 21 goals exactly to win the trophy.

Premier League Teams That Will Qualify for the UEFA Champions League

Leo Collis: With Chelsea, my mildly wild pick for Premier League winners, we've got three Champions League spots left to fill—ignoring any additional places awarded to English sides ahead of the 2027-28 tournament.

I'm predicting a bit of a drop-off from Manchester City, who will suffer a Pep Guardiola hangover that Enzo Maresca won't be able to remedy.

Meanwhile, Manchester United are never far from a crisis, and despite some apparent stability under Michael Carrick, that won't last much longer.

Arsenal will get in, no problem, and Liverpool's big signings from last season will finally start to shine under the tutelage of Andoni Iraola, with those two teams claiming two spots.

With that, I'm giving my final place to Tottenham Hotspur. That's right; I'm going for the team that finished two points clear of the drop last season.

Business has been good for Spurs in the summer, with the midfield entirely improved, a new center-back who won't find himself suspended every month, and a manager in Roberto de Zerbi who has previously proved adept at Premier League management.

Things are looking good at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and I'm saying that will lead to a surprising spot in the top four.

Nick Akerman: I think the ordering here is probably the bold bit.

I expect an Andoni Iraola-led Liverpool to finish ahead of Enzo Maresca's Man City. Although much of that relies on Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz remaining fit, the ex-Bournemouth manager is a clear communicator and should get his ideas across quickly to a Reds side that are gasping for new ideas after the malaise of Arne Slot's second year in charge. Maresca will need time to caress Pepisms into his style, despite their similarities.

Leo's excitement for Chelsea does seem worthy of further inspection. Xabi Alonso is an excellent man-manager who can drive underperforming teams to drastic improvement. He has a lot of really good players to work with.

The Spaniard's squad is rammed with options to overcome Man United, Aston Villa and other Champions League contenders who are going through mixed summers. I think they sneak in.

Calum Rogers: I've gone for Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United to join Arsenal in the top four, in that order.

I'm a little annoyed Nick has stolen my thunder on Liverpool, but Jérémy Jacquet looks like a strong addition defensively, and the Reds seem likely to make at least one splash signing in attack before the window closes that should aid in rebound seasons for Wirtz and Isak.

City could start slowly as they adjust to a post-Guardiola (and post-Rodri) world, and Maresca may have an impossible job in replacing the six-time Premier League winner. But I can't project a fall out of the top four for a team that has an attack featuring Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Antoine Semenyo, and with more additions looking likely elsewhere.

For the final spot, Chelsea and Tottenham came under consideration, but questions around the futures of Enzo Fernandez and seemingly several others in the squad make it hard to have confidence in the former, while the latter still need to prove that they can make it through a season without their squad being decimated by injuries.

Manchester United have had a quieter summer than both, but the midfield rebuild has been impressive, especially so if they add the physicality of Brighton & Hove Albion's Carlos Baleba to that unit.

The Athletic's David Ornstein has reported they're close to agreeing a deal for the 22-year-old, who would add steel to an exciting collection of technicians in Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and that improvement alongside an attack that led the league in goals after manager Michael Carrick took over in January may be enough to cover concerns about a defence that looks short on quality and depth.

Leo Collis: If you saw any of Switzerland's games at the 2026 World Cup, you might have caught a glimpse of Johan Manzambi's show-stealing performances.

He scored twice in an electric 20-minute cameo against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the group stages, and he backed that up with a goal and an assist against Canada from a starting berth.

He then provided an assist against Algeria in the round of 32, before being forced to sit out the rest of the tournament because of injury.

Aston Villa were obviously paying attention, fighting off a number of clubs to secure the 20-year-old's signature. Assuming he can put those injury woes behind him, Manzambi will light up the Premier League just like he did in the tournament in North America.

A change of the guard at Villa Park might be a hindrance, but he showed absolutely no fear of the big stage at his first World Cup, and he'll have no trouble bringing that energy, trickery, and clinical nature to the English top flight.

Nick Akerman: Midfielders are high on everyone's minds this summer. Transfer fees are so inflated that we've gotten to the point where £75 million for Bruno Guimarães seems like insane value, even if he's 28 years old (and I would ask, is 28 even old in modern football?)...

He's the best transfer in the league so far because of how well he fits what Arsenal needs. He's the finished article: a brilliant all-rounder, experienced captain and proven Premier League star.

Mikel Arteta is at the point where he's hunting all trophies, not just trying to land the domestic prize. Bruno is a trinket in a treasure chest already overflowing with gold.

The Brazilian will improve Arsenal in subtle ways. He and Declan Rice should be able to dovetail, interchanging as one bursts forward and the other holds. As we saw in the Community Shield, Bruno is more than capable of running things on his own, which is extremely important during a period in which Rice is juggling persistent injury issues.

In that sense, I can't see any other player being more ready to step in as the former Magpies hero.

Calum Rogers: Brentford smashed their transfer record to sign Mamadou Sangaré from RC Lens, and he looks like a player ready-made for the Premier League and for the Bees.

His energy levels will ensure he's able to handle the league's physicality, but his ability to break up play and quickly start attacks with a keen eye for a pass should pair well with Brentford's counter-attacking style.

Sangaré is not the finished product, but Brentford are the perfect club for him to make an immediate impact while working on his ability to manage and control games in midfield at the highest level.

This summer, we've seen several midfielders sold for fees around the £100 million mark, with elite clubs seemingly laser-focused on physical players like Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Elliot Anderson who can do a bit of everything.

Sangaré isn't there yet, but Brentford's exemplary track record in the transfer market is just another indicator that he could be something special.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

Leo Collis: Alejandro Garnacho gets away with one because he's only joined Aston Villa on loan, limiting the damage this transfer could do for the west Midlands.

Instead, I'm going for the eye-watering £40 million fee that Leeds United paid Manchester City for James Trafford, a goalkeeper who has never looked as convincing as the hype suggests.

When he was Burnley's No. 1 in the 2023-24 Premier League season, he wasn't comfortable under the high ball and didn't command his penalty box particularly well. Granted, he was only just entering his 20s at the time, but he didn't show much to suggest he would be on the fast-track to becoming a top-flight keeper, and the Clarets plummeted to the Championship.

After sealing a return to Manchester City for 2025-26, he was quickly demoted to the bench when Gianluigi Donnarumma became available. While that deal was difficult to pass up, it showed little confidence in the academy graduate and undoubtedly knocked his confidence.

There's still every chance he can develop into a solid stopper, but that much money for a player who has done little to impress seems like a massive waste of money for Leeds.

Nick Akerman: It was only in December 2025 when Crystal Palace decided to spend £35 million on Tottenham winger Brennan Johnson. Eight months later, he was the make-weight in a swap deal for Everton's Dwight McNeil, which included zero fees.

McNeil is a good player. But that's awful business on the Palace side, who have effectively taken £15 million's worth of a winger who didn't play much last season in exchange for their man who is younger, played at a higher standard, and is worth more.

What transfer strategy is this, other than pulling the ripcord on Johnson, who could have started afresh under Pierre Sage?

Calum Rogers: Newcastle United's summer can kindly be described as risky so far. No one represents that better than midfielder Aladji Bamba, who was signed from AS Monaco for a fee that could rise as high as £34 million, according to Ciaran Kelly of BBC Sport.

For a player who has played just 974 minutes of top-flight football, that is a staggering sum.

There is some promising data behind the Frenchman, who recorded two assists in his limited appearances. As Newcastle pointed out in their reporting of the signing, Bamba was top five in duels won (9.1 per game), tackles (3.6), successful take-ons (1.6) and aerial duels won (1.9) among Ligue 1 midfielders who played more than 500 minutes. And from the eye test, the youngster also clearly possesses the physicality typically required for the Premier League.

However, the small sample size makes those numbers difficult to project forward.

Newcastle have lost key leaders in his position in Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, focused on signing young players with limited experience to replace them, and hired a coach in Matthias Jaissle with no managerial history in a top European league.

Add it all up, and the chances of Bamba and the other additions making a successful transition to English football look slim.

David Ornstein of The Athletic has credited Newcastle with an interest in 24-year-old Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City, so hopefully the plan is to bring Bamba along slowly.

Even then, though, they have paid a hefty fee for an inexperienced player who faces an uphill battle to make an immediate impact.

Leo Collis: Brentford surprised everyone last season, earning their joint-best Premier League finish despite hiring an unproven manager and losing their starting goalkeeper, captain and two top scorers ahead of the campaign.

The Bees will get found out this time around, with teams being more wary of the threat posed by the potent but limited Igor Thiago and crowding out the big Brazilian's route to goal.

Sunderland will suffer a similar fate. Another surprise team in 2025-26, the Black Cats finished a remarkable seventh after earning promotion to the top flight from the Championship playoffs the season before.

That success could come back to haunt Regis Le Bris' side, as it will now have to deal with European football on top of another bruising Premier League campaign. With little investment in the squad so far this summer, there isn't enough quality to earn good results across both competitions, and their league form might suffer.

Finally, Hull City will have to be careful that their return to the top tier of English football doesn't end in humiliation. The Tigers' promotion was surprising in the first place, and despite the success of the promoted clubs last season, a lack of quality signings and a poor base to start with will condemn the Yorkshire side to a quick return to the Championship.

Nick Akerman: My picks mean Frank Lampard will keep Coventry City in the Premier League. I think it'll be close, but there's a good chance Fulham will become the next high-profile London side to follow West Ham into the Championship.

The Cottagers need to quickly adjust to life without Marco Silva. His management kept them safe during moments when they didn't look particularly great last season. New boss Álvaro Arbeloa made Real Madrid worse during his stint, and I think we'll see that on a larger scale here, given that Fulham isn't one of the best teams in the division, unlike Los Blancos in Spain.

Hull and Ipswich, I'm sorry. I just can't see them overcoming the mid-to-bottom pack, especially if the division plays out as brutally as it did last year.

Calum Rogers: I agree with Leo and Nick that Sunderland and Fulham are in danger, but remember earlier when I said I'm a coward? Well, I'm picking Hull, Coventry and Ipswich to get relegated.

But after a season that saw two promoted teams comfortably stay up and even qualify for Europe in Sunderland's case, maybe that's actually the boldest prediction someone could make? No? Well, I'm doing it anyway.

All three of the newbies have been busy, but it's just not enough...yet.

Hull have signed 11 players, but with the average age of those additions hovering around 22 years old, it's questionable whether they have added enough experience to truly make a go of surviving.

Coventry and Ipswich have brought in a decent mix of youth and experience.

The Sky Blues have added Gus Hamer and Taiwo Awoniyi, who have each previously recorded 10 goal contributions in a Premier League season, while the Tractor Boys' Julio Enciso and Abdul Fatawu are exciting young attackers who have shown glimpses of being able to have an impact in the division.

A couple of impact signings could still turn the tide, but I'm sticking with the promoted trio as my relegation picks for now.

Leo Collis: Pep Guardiola has left big shoes to fill at Manchester City. The Catalan won pretty much everything available to him during a decade at the Etihad Stadium, and despite the clear spending capital available, he was still pivotal in molding the squad into an all-conquering juggernaut.

Enzo Maresca comes in with a relatively light CV. He had just a season-and-a-half at Chelsea before his controversial departure, earning a fourth-place Premier League finish in his first season and then leaving Stamford Bridge with the club just fifth in the English top flight. A Conference League title and a Club World Cup look good in the trophy cabinet, but they are minor trophies in the grand scheme of things.

With Manchester City, he'll struggle to impose himself on a squad that only just said goodbye to the influential Guardiola, and the results will suffer. The talent is clearly still available—although the imminent departure of Rodri is a huge loss—but the 46-year-old won't be able to accentuate their abilities as his mentor could.

Consequently, City will slip out of title contention, won't make the top four, and could even struggle to finish in the top six.

Nick Akerman: Michael Carrick pretty much backed Man United into a corner after his excellent stint as interim boss led them to a Champions League place.

It would have been bold for the board to hire someone else full-time, just in case the alternative failed and accusations that Carrick never received his opportunity came their way.

While Carrick's extended tenure was a given, few supporters will be happy with how he's being backed in the transfer market. We're one week away from United's first match of the season, and Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are the club's big midfield signings (with Carlos Baleba likely to come soon). Good deals if taken at face value, but not enough.

Where's the next left back? Where's the competition for Benjamin Sesko up front? How is United seriously on the verge of lining up with the same creaking defense they had in 2022?

Carrick showed signs of tactical naivety at times, but was bailed out by players in great form. He is now under much greater pressure. I think it could go wrong at speed, hastened by a twitchy INEOS who may be quick to move on if the new boss turns out to be another pretender.

Calum Rogers: Jeez, an awful lot of negativity here, guys. Haven't you heard that preseason is the time when every team has hope?

I guess it's on me to send the readers off with a feel-good prediction, so here goes nothing: Brentford will finish in the top six.

How you feel about this likely comes down to your take on Brentford winning just one of their final 10 games last season, tumbling from as high as fifth in January to a ninth-place finish and missing out on European qualification on goal difference.

Did the league figure them out? Or did a thin squad just run out of steam and a bit of luck?

Clearly, I'm going with the latter, and Brentford's summer business looks to have addressed the depth problem. Callum Wilson and Jaidon Anthony provide options for rotation and can change games off the bench, while I've already explained how excited I am about Sangaré in midfield.

With so much upheaval at the top end of the table, and with other usual top-six challengers like Aston Villa and Newcastle also losing significant players, there's another opportunity for a smaller club to follow in Bournemouth's footsteps from last season, and Brentford look the most likely to me.

Leo Collis: It's clear I haven't learned my lesson from last season , when I picked Chelsea to win the title off the back of a convincing Club World Cup win.

There has been no such silverware heading into the 2026-27 campaign, and the Blues are coming off a season in which they finished a distant 10th in the Premier League. That makes this pick even more ludicrous.

But with new manager Xabi Alonso in the dugout, things feel quite hopeful. Meanwhile, some shrewd signings, including the excellent Morgan Rogers, in addition to some much-needed experience in the dressing room courtesy of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, should change the atmosphere at Stamford Bridge for the better.

With European football off the calendar, the Blues can focus their attention on a strong domestic campaign. With Arsenal perhaps prioritizing a first European Cup title in club history, that could play nicely into Chelsea's hands.

Honestly, Arsenal should be going back-to-back. But we're in the business of bold, and much like last season, bold is blue.

Nick Akerman: I swear I'm not doing this on purpose. I realize picking Arsenal to win the title right now is like saying night will turn to day.

Mikel Arteta's squad are by far the deepest and best-prepped in the Premier League. Defending the crown is non-negotiable, and to be honest, success should be measured by whether or not the Gunners finally win the Champions League, because the rest of the English clubs are just not in a position to compete with them.

So, to get bold with it, I think there's a genuine chance Arsenal could win the title with the highest-ever gap to second place.

Manchester City's 2017-18 Centurions currently hold the record, finishing 19 points ahead of rivals Manchester United. Arteta's side won't reach 100 points, but their nearest rivals are all dealing with issues that may lead to inconsistency. Let's go with a 20-point title win for the North Londoners.

Calum Rogers: Arsenal have made upgrades to a title-winning team. Christos Tzolis looks to have added more juice to the team's attack, while the addition of Bruno Guimarães affords manager Mikel Arteta more options both tactically and in terms of rotation.

The Athletic's David Ornstein, Jacob Tanswell and James McNicholas have also reported that Arsenal have agreed a deal for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, which would add to an already deep defensive unit. The 28-year-old England international will also help cover for the injured William Saliba, who will be out until around October with a back injury.

There are still concerns in attack, namely over the fitness of Bukayo Saka and whether Viktor Gyökeres can offer a more consistent threat, and perhaps there will be a lull after the emotionally draining chase for a first league title since 2004. While I still think Arsenal have enough to repeat, my somewhat spicy take is that they will do so with fewer points than the 85 they recorded last season.

articles.title: Akron Football Reveals Finalists to Serve as OC for 1st Drive of Season Opener
articles.summary: It's usually headline news when an NFL or college football team narrows its list of coaching candidates to a group of finalists.
articles.body:
It's usually headline news when an NFL or college football team narrows its list of coaching candidates to a group of finalists.

Akron just did that, although it comes with a bit of a twist.

The Zips revealed the list of finalists for their "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" promotion that will let one season-ticket holder work with head coach Joe Moorhead to script the plays for the home opener against Robert Morris on Sept. 12.

Athletic director Andrew Goodrich called the finalists to break the news:

Notably, one of the finalists is Dan Katz, the co-host of Pardon My Take . He revealed he purchased 18 season tickets to increase his chances at winning the promotion:

Earlier this month, Akron announced the promotion that automatically entered every season-ticket holder into a random drawing for what it described as "the first-ever opportunity to help script the opening drive of the football team's home season opener."

It should be noted the winner will get to work with Moorhead to design the plays and won't have full autonomy. With that in mind, don't expect a fake punt on the first play of the game or an 85-yard field goal attempt.

After all, Akron is still trying to win the game.

"We're always looking for new ways to bring our fans closer to the program," Goodrich said. "This is about giving one of our most loyal supporters a seat at the table, right alongside our coaching staff, on the biggest night of the season."

Akron is coming off a 5-7 season, which was its best mark since the 2017 campaign. A one-game improvement could put it in a bowl game, so the coaching staff will be under slightly more pressure in 2026.

Perhaps the guest offensive coordinator will deliver a touchdown and help set the stage for a bowl season.

articles.title: Giménez, capitán hasta el final
articles.standfirst: El uruguayo, con su futuro en el aire, trabaja con la máxima intensidad y está muy pendiente de jóvenes y recién llegados
articles.summary: El uruguayo, con su futuro en el aire, trabaja con la máxima intensidad y está muy pendiente de jóvenes y recién llegados
articles.body: Si alguien sabe lo que es llegar al Atlético muy joven y tener que hacerse hueco en un vestuario de máximo nivel, ese es José María Giménez. El uruguayo llegó al cuadro rojiblanco justo antes de que los de Simeone ganasen la primera Liga de la era Cholo. Un equipo que contaba en sus filas con dos futbolistas como Godín y Miranda. Dos jugadores que marcaron el carácter y la manera de comportarse de Josema. Dos centrales de mucho nivel que enseñaron al uruguayo una forma de entender un vestuario que todavía sigue presente. Con su futuro en el aire, Giménez es uno de los futbolistas señalados para salir del Atlético este verano. Algo que no ha afectado al charrúa a la hora de comportarse. Desde que regresó del Mundial, Josema ha estado muy pendiente de todos los canteranos y de las caras nuevas del Atlético. “Ejerce de capitán aunque no juegue. Él siempre ha respetado mucho las jerarquías, algo que aprendió de líderes como Godín”, aseguran quienes viven el día a día con Josema. Y es que, desde el primer momento, se le ha visto muy comprometido con todos los recién llegados. En el viaje a Corea se pudo comprobar que uno de los capitanes rojiblancos iba a acoger pronto a Kang-in Lee en el grupo. El propio futbolista coreano le agradeció la confianza con un abrazo tras anotar su primer gol como rojiblanco. “Me dijo que iba a salir y que iba a marcar, y quise ir a agradecerle la confianza”, señaló Kang-in a la conclusión del choque ante el Málaga. Giménez, que, a pesar de partir como quinto central ahora mismo, tras Pubill, Cuti Romero, Hancko y Le Normand, no ha cambiado su manera de comportarse. Ante el Málaga se le pudo ver muy enchufado en el banquillo y dando ánimos a sus compañeros. Algo que es habitual en cada entrenamiento. En la sesión del jueves, la primera tras el debut del equipo, Josema formó pareja en defensa con Cuti Romero. El uruguayo fue uno de los más destacados de la sesión, con varias acciones defensivas que recibieron elogios de todos sus compañeros. "¡Buena, Pela!". Una frase que se pudo escuchar varias veces a lo largo del entrenamiento. Es evidente que Giménez no ha comenzado su 15.ª temporada como posiblemente le gustaría, pero no por ello ha modificado su actitud. Queda semana y media para que se cierre el mercado de fichajes y su situación sigue abierta, pero no parece que Josema vaya a dejarse llevar. Seguirá ejerciendo de capitán hasta el final.

articles.title: Diomande: "Estoy preparado para morir por Mourinho"
articles.standfirst: El nuevo jugador del Real Madrid ha hablado por primera vez como jugador blanco para Sporty TV
articles.summary: El nuevo jugador del Real Madrid ha hablado por primera vez como jugador blanco para Sporty TV
articles.body: Yan Diomande, fichaje estrella del Real Madrid este verano, ha concedido una entrevista a SportyTV en la que hablado de cómo se produjo su fichaje, cómo fue la llamada de José Mourinho y explica los consejos que recibió de Didier Drogba tras conocer su llegada al conjunto blanco. El jugador dice estar "orgulloso y feliz porque he hecho mi sueño realidad". Su objetivo siempre ha sido ser el mejor jugador del mundo y sigue persiguiéndolo. Se considera alguien humilde, pero seguro de si mismo. "No hay club más grande que el Madrid. Ellos gastaron mucho dinero en mí, pero no tengo ninguna presión. ¿Por qué debería tener miedo? Voy hacer lo que pueda en el campo y Dios hará el resto". Nunca olvidará su reacción cuando se enteró que el Madrid quería ficharlo: "Fue como un sueño porque no hay club más grande. Desde que lo supe, no dormí. No podía creerlo. Hablé con Juni y luego hablé con el míster. Me sorprendió porque hablaba francés. Mourinho se levantó a las 5 de la mañana para hablar conmigo. Eso significa que es importante. Cuando el Madrid te llama no puedes decir que no, así que dije: 'Si me quieren, allí voy a estar". También recuerda cuales fueron las primeras palabras de Mou: "Nada más llegar me dijo: 'Te prometí que ibas a ser parte de mi equipo y aquí estás'. Y yo le dije: 'Estoy feliz de trabajar contigo porque eres el mejor'. Puedo aprender mucho de él, es el entrenador adecuado para seguir con mi formación. Estoy preparado para morir por él". Dentro del vestuario también tiene buena relación con Vinicius: "Ya había hablado con él antes. Es la única persona con la que soy cercana. También con Mbappé porque hablamos el mismo idioma. Me cae bien todo el mundo. Todos son amables conmigo". Resulta curioso recordar que Diomande debutó como profesional contra el Madrid en el Bernabéu: "Es cosa de Dios. Yo creo mucho en Dios. Y ha sido mucha coincidencia. Solo quiero disfrutar cada día. De ese partido recuerdo cambiar la camiseta con Mbappé y hoy estamos en el mismo vestuario riéndonos juntos. Nunca olvidaré al Leganés porque fue el único club que me dio la oportunidad de mostrar mi calidad". Pero antes del Leganés, el futbolista pasó una etapa en Estados Unidos: "Fue una buena decisión. Era joven y me lo pasaba bien. Como chico africano no tienes muchas oportunidades de viajar. Era divertido porque viajaba mucho y jugaba al fútbol. Nunca olvidaré mi camino". Diomande es ya un icono en el fútbol africano, pero antes de él el continente tenía otras leyendas: "Mis ídolos eran Yaya Touré y Drogba. Hablé con él hace dos días y me dijo que Mourinho era como su padre, que tuviese cuidado. Tienes que trabajar duro, pero es un buen tipo. Fue una leyenda y sigue siéndolo así que le tienes que escuchar. Y es bueno hablar con ellos porque puedo aprender mucho con ellos. Es verdad que no le hice muchas preguntas porque soy tímido. Todavía soy joven y tengo que mostrar mi personalidad". Por último, el jugador ha hablado de su paso por el Mundial: "Fue una buena experiencia. Era mi primer Mundial. No esperábamos ganar, pero fue un buen torneo. Le doy gracias a todos por la pasión para hacerlo mejor. Estoy orgulloso de ser el jugador más joven en jugar un Mundial para mi país. Y eso me hace trabajar más duro". Durante la Copa del Mundo, su historia se hizo conocida, después de que publicase una carta abierta a su hermana fallecida: "Me impulsa a no rendirme nunca y a seguir trabajando duro para hacer realidad mi sueño. Fue el momento perfecto para compartir mi historia. Todo lo que hago es por ella".

images.caption: José Mourinho charla con Diomandé, Mbappé, Konaté y Cucurella.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso no se atreve a confirmar la continuidad de Enzo
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Chelsea evitó contestar a las preguntas emitidas sobre las intenciones del técnico argentino
articles.summary: El técnico del Chelsea evitó contestar a las preguntas emitidas sobre las intenciones del técnico argentino
articles.body: Se sigue respirando una cierta calma tensa alrededor de la figura de Enzo Fernández. Todavía restan poco más de 10 días para que cierre el mercado y ni el mismo Xabi Alonso se atreve a ofrecer una respuesta contundente sobre el futuro del centrocampista argentino. La semana pasada, recordemos, The Athletic sacó a la luz un supuesto 'ultimatum' del Chelsea al Manchester City para fichar a Enzo Fernández. "No vamos a hacer nada", respondía un Enzo Maresca en la previa de la Community Shield. Dicha supuesta amenaza caducó el pasado fin de semana... mientras Stamford Bridge sometió a un juicio público al ex de River o Benfica en el amistoso contra la Real Sociedad. No son pocos los frentes que tiene abiertos Xabi Alonso en esta recta final de mercado. Pero el nombre de Enzo Fernández sigue copando la mayoría de titulares. De hecho, en la previa del estreno de la Premier League 25-26 contra el Fulham de su amigo Arbeloa, se le ha insistido bastante sobre este aspecto al tolosarra. "Enzo es un jugador del Chelsea y de primerísimo nivel. Está entrenando muy bien desde que se incorporó al equipo hace 10 días y está muy integrado. Estamos contentos con él y se está preparando para el lunes", contestó Xabi Alonso. Sin embargo, cuando le preguntaron si le había mostrado su intención de quedarse, trató de esquivar la pregunta. "Está entrenando muy bien. Tiene una buena actitud y eso es lo que queremos. Se está preparando al máximo para el inicio de la Premier". Por tanto, salvo sorpresa mayúscula, se espera que Enzo Fernández esté presente en la convocatoria del Chelsea para visitar al Fulham el próximo lunes. Será un debut tremendamente especial para Xabi Alonso a los mandos de este Chelsea. Y es que, en el banquillo de al lado en Craven Cottage, se encontrará con su amigo Arbeloa. "Por supuesto que podemos tener una relación. Pero, una vez que estemos en el campo, no hay amigos. Lucharemos durante los 90 minutos por el interés de cada club".

articles.title: Cuestión de liderazgo
articles.standfirst: Flick quiere a Rodri por su fútbol, pero también para que sea un de los jefes del equipo
articles.summary: Flick quiere a Rodri por su fútbol, pero también para que sea un de los jefes del equipo
articles.body: La llegada de Rodrigo Hernández supone un cambio de paradigma en el presente azulgrana. El ex del Manchester City, campeón de todos los títulos posibles con el conjunto británico y de Mundial, Eurocopa y Nations League con la selección española, ha aterrizado en el vestuario del Barça con los galones suficientes para ser el líder que guíe a los jóvenes de la plantilla a conquistar, de nuevo, la ansiada Champions League y mantener la hegemonía a nivel nacional. La salida de Robert Lewandowski tras unos años de liderazgo en el vestuario, supuso perder un referente en los grandes partidos. El polaco, tirando de veteranía, era el que muchas ocasiones ponía calma y aconsejaba a los jugadores jóvenes en momentos donde algo fallaba o el nerviosismo se apoderaba. Además, en este mercado también ha salido Ronald Araujo dirección Liverpool. El uruguayo, con menos protagonismo en el césped, ejercía de hermano mayor para muchos chicos y era una de las personas más queridas dentro del vestuario, además de ser uno de los portadores del brazalete de capitán. Si a esto le sumamos la marcha de Ter Stegen, en el cuerpo técnico tenían claro que necesitaban a un jerarca al lado de Raphinha, a una persona que orientara al equipo dentro y, sobre todo, fuera del terreno de juego. Lo que sale de la Ciudad Deportiva Joan Gamper horas después de la llegada de Rodri es un mensaje claro: “Hemos fichado a un líder”. Y eso es lo que quería, y por lo que ha luchado, un Fick que respira con esta incorporación. Tener un capitán, en principio, sin brazalete. La reestructuración en la capitanía es total. La temporada pasada los capitanes eran Ter Stegen, Araujo, De Jong, Raphinha y Pedri. Dos de estos cinco están fuera del club y Hansi Flick ha decidido quitarle ese poder provisional al neerlandés hasta que vuelva de lesión o se hagan las votaciones finales cuando la plantilla esté cerrada. "Hasta que eso suceda, Raphinha será el capitán, junto a Eric y Gavi", comentó el germano en declaraciones al club.  Con el ascenso de Raphinha a primer capitán y la incorporación de Eric y Gavi, se hace difícil pensar que Rodri pueda optar a portar el brazalete, aunque la última palabra la tendrán unos futbolistas que ven al centrocampista madrileño como un referente.

articles.title: Mastantuono: "En el Real Madrid no fue un año fácil"
articles.standfirst: "No es una revancha, sino una oportunidad para intentar demostrar el jugador que soy"
articles.summary: "No es una revancha, sino una oportunidad para intentar demostrar el jugador que soy"
articles.body: El jugador argentino del Fiorentina Franco Mastantuono dijo este jueves que la pasada temporada en el Real Madrid "no fue fácil" y que en el club italiano, al que llegó cedido, tiene la oportunidad de demostrar su nivel como futbolista. "En el Madrid tuvimos una temporada complicada todos, no fue un año fácil, pero, como digo siempre, estas cosas ayudan a mejorar, a aprender y a pensar que siempre se puede mejorar, que siempre hay margen de mejora en el fútbol", afirmó el argentino en su primera rueda de prensa como jugador 'viola'. "No es una revancha, sino una oportunidad para intentar demostrar el jugador que soy y para ayudar al Fiorentina", declaró. Mastantuono reveló que la conversación con el club blanco sobre su salida fue "muy cordial y amistosa", y que eligió el equipo toscano entre muchas opciones porque el proyecto le impresionó "mucho". "Una semana antes del anuncio tomé esta decisión y estoy muy contento", aseveró, y agregó que siente el compromiso de llevar al Fiorentina "a la cima". El jugador, que subrayó "el privilegio" de haber jugado tanto en el Real Madrid como en el River Plate, dijo que los aficionados 'gigliati' le recibieron de una manera "increíble". "Me han dado mucho cariño y eso me recuerda a mi casa, Argentina. Estaba jugando en la playa y me divertí con algunos chicos que estaban allí. Para mí es normal estar con amigos y familia y jugar en la playa", recalcó. Mastantuono destacó la figura del mítico jugador argentino Gabriel Batistuta, una leyenda del Fiorentina, y añadió que le gustaría hacer historia en el club como él. "Jugó aquí e hizo algo increíble. Pero también hay compañeros que han pasado por aquí y con los que he compartido vestuario, como Martínez Quarta y Nico González. He hablado con ellos y me han hablado maravillas del ambiente", mantuvo. "No me propongo objetivos, quiero ayudar al equipo y mejorar día a día", concluyó. En total, en la temporada 2025-2026, Mastantuono, de 19 años, disputó con el Real Madrid 1.484 minutos en 35 partidos, 17 de ellos como titular, y consiguió tres goles entre todas las competiciones.

articles.title: Tennessee Reveals 'Neyland Legacy' Uniforms in New Video, Photos for 2026 CFB Season
articles.summary: Having already named their home stadium after Hall of Fame head coach Robert Neyland, the Tennessee Volunteers are incorporating his legacy into their uniforms for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Having already named their home stadium after Hall of Fame head coach Robert Neyland, the Tennessee Volunteers are incorporating his legacy into their uniforms for the 2026 season.

The Vols revealed the "Neyland Legacy" uniforms they will add to their rotation for the upcoming season.

Some of the Neyland-specific aspects of the design include a patch on the left shoulder in the image of him kneeling, similar to the Neyland statue that sits outside of their home stadium.

The helmet design is based off the leather model the Vols used in the very-early days of the football program.

Neyland spent a total of 21 seasons as Tennessee's head coach across three different stints between 1926 to '52. He also had multiple stints in the military as a member of the Army, including in 1941 during World War II.

Tennessee went 173-31-12 and won four national titles during Neyland's tenure. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1956.

The Volunteers will kickoff the 2026 season at Neyland Stadium against Furman on Sept. 5 at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.standfirst: El delantero mallorquín pondrá rumbo a la capital para formar parte del filial rojiblanco por una cesión con opción de compra.
articles.summary: El delantero mallorquín pondrá rumbo a la capital para formar parte del filial rojiblanco por una cesión con opción de compra.
articles.body: Marc Domenech abandonará la isla rumbo a la capital de España para recalar en el Atlético Madrileño. Mallorca y Atlético llevan negociando desde inicio de semana por el futbolista y, tal y como avanzó Radio Marca Baleares, pasará a formar parte del filial rojiblanco. Será en forma de cesión con opción de compra. El joven delantero de 19 años pondrá rumbo a Madrid en las próximas horas para pasar las pruebas médicas. Tras un ascenso meteórico desde el Juvenil del San Francisco a Primera División con el Mallorca y un paso mejorable por Ceuta en forma de cesión, el de Llucmajor buscará crecer a las órdenes de Fernando Torres en 1 RFEF para volver a encontrar su mejor versión. El espejo donde mirarse es Arnau Ortiz que, tras jugar en la Primera División Polaca, recaló en el filial rojiblanco y ayer debutó en La Liga como titular en el estreno liguero de los del Cholo ante el Málaga.
